Class PacketMonitorService

java.lang.Object
com.meshtastic.client.service.PacketMonitorService
public final class PacketMonitorService extends Object
Captures and stores LoRa mesh packets for the packet monitor window. The service owns the handoff from protocol runtimes, durable storage in the local database, and live event delivery to UI listeners. Public methods may be called from arbitrary threads. Operations that touch the database or shared service state are synchronized on the service instance.

    • recordRawIncoming

      public void recordRawIncoming(String connectionId, String packetType, String payloadText, byte[] packetBytes)
      Records an incoming raw protocol packet that is not a Meshtastic protobuf.

      This is used by the MeshCore Companion Protocol. The monitor stores the raw bytes, a HEX/ASCII preview, and a human-readable packet type without attempting to convert the payload into a MeshProtos.MeshPacket.

      Parameters:
      connectionId - connection identifier in ConnectionManager
      packetType - raw packet type used by the UI filter
      payloadText - short payload description
      packetBytes - original packet bytes

    • forEachMatchingBatch

      public long forEachMatchingBatch(PacketMonitorService.PacketQuery query, int batchSize, PacketMonitorService.PacketBatchConsumer consumer) throws IOException
      Streams all packets that match the filter in fixed-size batches. This is intended for operations such as export, where loading the entire result set into memory would be unnecessary or unsafe.
      Parameters:
      query - table filter; null means no additional conditions
      batchSize - maximum number of rows in one batch
      consumer - callback that receives batches in captured_at DESC, id DESC order
      Returns:
      actual number of processed entries
      Throws:
      IOException - if the consumer fails or database rows cannot be read

    • loadPageFrame

      public PacketMonitorService.PacketPage loadPageFrame(PacketMonitorService.PacketQuery query, int offset, int limit)
      Loads a fixed table frame by offset in the global captured_at DESC, id DESC. The UI uses this for step-by-step navigation between equal-sized pages.
      Parameters:

      offset - offset from the start of the result set; 0 is the newest page
      limit - frame size
      Returns:
